tasks.title: Scarlet Badis in Aquariums
tasks.transcript: It looks like a cartoon character, but it is the real-life scarlet badis, a freshwater fish only about two centimeters long. In the wild, it generally lives peacefully in the slow-moving streams of India. Exploring, it is a popular choice for aquariums. In captive environments, however, males are more aggressive. They chase and nip at other males that enter their territory, so it is crucial to include plenty of vegetation. Plants act as hiding places and boundaries between males' territories. Male scarlet badis are a vivid orange-red, or scarlet, with light bluish stripes. When a male is not confronting another male, his color is less bright and can almost resemble the dull gray coloring of a female. This can make the sexes difficult to distinguish, although any visible scarlet indicates a male. Unlike in most fish species, males are also usually slightly larger than females. A male shows his brightest coloring during the breeding season. In aquariums, he may perform a kind of dance to impress a female, following her until she decides whether to mate with him.
